resumen: The squat with your own body: you go down bending hips and knees with the torso upright, and stand back up. It is the base for learning the movement before adding load.
ejecucion: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart or slightly wider, toes turned slightly out.
Reach your arms out in front or cross your hands in front of your chest for balance.
Go down by pushing your hips back and down while bending your knees, which follow the direction of your feet, with your chest up.
Go as low as you can keep your back straight and your heels down, ideally with your thighs parallel to the floor or a little lower.
Stand up by pushing the floor with your whole foot. If your heels lift or your knees cave in, go less deep.
matices: A review of squat biomechanics reports that stopping the knees from travelling past the toes forces more forward lean and increases the demand on the hips; so there is no need to avoid it as long as the heels stay down. Without weight, it is mainly an exercise for learning the movement and for beginners; to keep progressing, add load or move on to single-leg variations.
